Data-shaped designs: the actual Buyout (25 vintages, 383 funds) and VC (27 vintages, 432 funds) vintage calendars and fund counts up to 2010, the historical factor path, exact pricing at $\beta_{MKT}=1$ with mean-one lognormal deal shocks (monthly $\sigma$ 0.130 Buyout, 0.154 VC), 15 deals per fund, quarterly cash flows. Estimates minimize the criterion over the admissible domain (as in the empirical tables). Bias and RMSE against the true value; SD across replications. Rej.: rejection of the structural value $\beta_{MKT}=1$ at 5\% with the empirical tables' inference (Bartlett sandwich, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$, fixed-$b$ critical values), among interior tested draws (all 1{,}000 draws interior for L2 VYP and $U_{v,H}$ at $H\le20$ yr; 999--1{,}000 at 30 yr). We reserve ``size'' for a valid null: at $H=0$, L2 VYP rejects $\beta_{MKT}=1$ in 4.1\% (Buyout) and 6.3\% (VC) of draws, but rejects its own criterion target $\theta_0^\dagger$ in 13.1\% and 34.9\% because positive target shift and negative finite-sample bias partially offset at $\beta_{MKT}=1$. Outer vintage weights for $U_{v,H}$: $q_v=1$ weights each eligible ($n_v\ge 2$) vintage year equally (main specification), whereas $q_v=n_v$ weights each vintage proportionally to its fund count $n_v$. For $U_{v,H}$ with $q_v=n_v$ the rejection rate is in brackets: it shows why the empirical tables report no inference for that weighting. Monte Carlo SE of the bias 0.002--0.011; of rejection rates 0.7 points at a 5\% rate with 1{,}000 tested draws (observed-rate MCSE across printed cells: 0.14--1.55 points).}
